brokers.thesis: Managed the gRevlimid transition with niche launches; US sales +5% CAGR FY26-28E; injectables, 505(b)(2), transdermals, NCEs, biosimilars and vaccines over 2-3 years
India and EM outperform, but North America fell for a second quarter; EPS only ~5% CAGR FY26-28; higher D&A, interest and tax
Post-Q1FY27 outlook (report behind a login; only the rating and target are public)
gRevlimid and Mirabegron (~36% of US sales) erode; revenue/EBITDA CAGR 7%/-1% over two years despite 17% non-US growth
All-round growth; integration costs weigh on near-term margins; a quick ramp-up of innovation could re-rate
Upgrade to Buy on a pipeline-led rerating (Business Today)

moat: #1 in oncology in India; 78 brands above Rs25 cr (56 in 2022); 7,000+ reps; chronic share 54.2%; grew 15-20% vs IPM ~10%
Pricing is regulated and trade generics grow; but differentiated launches (biosimilars, NCEs, semaglutide device) keep it ahead
Two in-house NCEs on the Indian market (saroglitazar, desidustat), 16 biosimilars approved in India, 16 vaccines licensed, a US NDA under priority review
Unusual for an Indian generics company; still small in revenue outside India
#3 by US generic prescriptions; ranked in the top three in ~60% of its product families; 274 products marketed
US generics is a price-taker business; the windfalls (gRevlimid, Mirabegron) were not the moat and are fading
Every USFDA inspection since Mar-2025 closed with an EIR (VAI/NAI), including Jarod, previously a problem site
Clean now, but one bad inspection can freeze launches
Consumer segment earned only Rs267 cr of profit in FY26 on Rs3,954 cr revenue after acquisition costs
Amplitude: ~EUR100 mn French orthopaedics; 20%+ EBITDA before acquisition accounting
Segment loss of Rs178 cr in FY26; no scale advantage yet
critiques: US erosion is the overhang: gRevlimid and Mirabegron were ~36% of US sales and both fade; new launches unlikely to fill the gap fully
EPS grows only ~5% a year FY26-28 even as revenue compounds; D&A, interest and tax rise after the acquisitions
North America declined for a second straight quarter on competition in base products, despite a strong launch pace
Integration of acquisitions will weigh on near-term margins; a re-rating needs the innovation business to scale quickly
Operating cash flow fell to ~Rs2,100 cr in FY26 against ~Rs8,500 cr of EBITDA (Mirabegron payout, acquisition working capital)
Rs7,000+ cr of acquisitions in 12 months across medtech, consumer, CDMO and US specialty: breadth over focus
gaps: gRevlimid's sales by year (never disclosed): we cannot compute an ex-gRevlimid forward P/E median (only the combined gRevlimid + Mirabegron estimates from JM, ~36% of US sales, and PL, >45% of FY25 EPS, exist).
